Subject: Unit economics deep-dive & pricing follow-up

Hi Alex / Jamie —

Great to meet you both today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Goals: Reduce inference spend while preserving accuracy for customer-facing scoring and recommendation features. Target: < $1M inference spend/year for initial rollout; scale after pilot.

2) Workload profile (your inputs): ~100M API tokens/month initially (prompt + completion tokens), 60% chat-like interactive queries, 40% batch scoring. Latency SLOs: p95 < 200ms for interactive.

3) Key asks from FintechX for qualification:
   - Target unit cost target: $/1M tokens goal (you mentioned $350–$450 per 1M tokens in the call)
   - Expected monthly active users and avg features/events per user (you said ~200k MAU, ~3 calls/user/day)
   - CAC / monetization cadence to model payback (we discussed 6–9 month payback targets)

4) Next steps (for this thread):
   A) I'll share a lightweight unit-econ model and two price scenarios (hosted API vs dedicated reserved capacity) — attachment: redwood_unit_econ_model.xlsx
   B) Please confirm the 100M tokens/mo estimate and your target $/1M token range (budget band) so we can produce a tailored quote and $/feature analysis.
   C) If procurement wants an SOW/quote we can include a pilot pricing line (1–3 months) and expected ramp plan.

I attached a modeling workbook and will follow up with a short note comparing hosted vs dedicated economics and CAC payback examples. Looping Nikhil (pricing) for any follow-up pricing questions.

Thanks —

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 100M tokens/mo is a conservative starting point for Pilot A (US customers). If pilot goes well we expect to double within 6 months.
- The $350–$450 per 1M tokens range is what our finance team has penciled for the first year, but we have flexibility if we see strong unit-econ upside.
- For CAC/payback: our target is 6 months for new features; anything that pushes payback beyond 9 months becomes a tougher sell to the board.

Can you produce a short $/feature example? Specifically: given 100M tokens/mo, what does that translate to per-unique-feature served (we have ~5 primary features that call the model), and what margin would you expect vs a baseline price? Also, Jamie from procurement will need an initial SOW/quote to start legal procurement.

Appreciate it — talk soon.

Alex — perfect, thanks for the clarity. Attached is a simple summary and the model (redwood_unit_econ_model.xlsx). High level takeaways below so you have a quick read: 

Summary (assumptions: 100M tokens/mo, 5 features, 3 calls/user/day, expected ramp to 200M in 6 months):
- Hosted API scenario: list-price blended cost ~ $420 / 1M tokens (includes model tier and streaming). With typical batching/caching we estimate effective cost to FintechX ~ $320 / 1M tokens after expected optimizations (prefix caching, quantized model variant for batch jobs).
- Dedicated reserved scenario (12mo commit): effective cost can drop to ~$220–$260 / 1M tokens at 100M–200M tokens/mo depending on GPU type and KV cache hit-rate. Upfront commit and flexible burst required.

$/feature example (pilot month, 100M tokens):
- 100M tokens / 5 features = 20M tokens per feature/month (avg)
- At $320 / 1M tokens -> $320 * 20 = $6,400 per feature/month
- Annualized (x12) = ~$76,800 per feature/year

CAC/payback illustration (simple):
- If a new feature generates $30k ARR on average in year 1, at $76.8k cost per feature/year the margin is negative. The lever to improve payback is: lower inference $/1M (move to dedicated or quantized), reduce tokens per feature (client-side caching / more selective calls), or increase revenue per feature. 

Target margin guidance:
- For a healthy product margin target of 40% contribution margin on feature revenue, inference unit cost needs to be ~ <$120–$150 per 1M tokens given the example revenue profile. That maps to dedicated + strong caching/quantization or a hybrid routing policy.

Attachments in the workbook: a) hosted vs dedicated line-item calc, b) $/feature sensitivity table, c) 6–9 month CAC payback scenarios. 

Next asks for you:
1) Confirm whether the $350–$450 band is internal target or external budget band (so we price accordingly).
2) If procurement prefers a pilot SOW (1–3 months) we can draft a short SOW and a pilot quote (I’ve attached a one-page SOW draft for initial review). Attachment: fintechx_sow_draft.pdf

Looping Nikhil and Rishi to provide a formal quote & recommended SKU mapping based on your region and anticipated GPU footprint. We can include a staged pricing table to preserve flexibility as volume ramps.

Best —

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
